2611.29702.abstract: Unresolved companions alter the luminosity and spectra of a star, but a colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) reveals them only when the system is over-luminous, and a Gaia photocentre orbit constrains only a combination of the mass and flux ratios. We fit the absolute Gaia BP/RP (XP) and SPHEREx spectra (XPS) of about 71,000 low-mass stars in the Gaia Catalogue of Nearby Stars with the J-CaPS XPS emulator, which predicts single-star and coeval-binary spectra on an absolute flux scale. First, more than half of known binaries lie within the main-sequence (MS) band of the CMD, because the companion is faint or lifts a metal-poor primary onto the single-star ridge. XPS recovers 86 per cent of the binaries that a CMD cut finds and 44 per cent of those it misses. Second, a small photocentre motion can come from a faint companion or a luminous one of nearly equal mass. XPS distinguishes them and recovers the mass ratios of double-lined binaries. Among substellar candidates with radial-velocity follow-up, it ranks all 11 binaries above all 16 confirmed brown-dwarf or planet hosts. The public package spbin provides this check before follow-up. Third, where XPS detects no companion light, we place an upper limit on the light of an MS companion. Among Gaia DR3 astrometric orbits with clean spectral fits, 2841 require more companion mass than XPS allows for a single MS star. Within 200 pc, their companion masses cluster at those of typical white dwarfs, and nearly circular orbits support this interpretation. Of 24 companions that joint radial-velocity and astrometric orbits show to be faint, XPS recovers 22, compared with 14 selected by the absence of a colour excess. Applied to forthcoming Gaia DR4 orbital solutions, XPS can help distinguish luminous binaries from substellar companions and identify candidate compact companions whose dynamical masses exceed the limits allowed by their light.

2611.30001.abstract: Abell 1060 is a nearby, dynamically relaxed galaxy cluster hosting the extended radio structure Flying Fox (FF) near its center. We used high-resolution XRISM/Resolve spectroscopy to measure intracluster medium (ICM) motions and velocity dispersion. Spatially resolved analysis reveals a velocity gradient of approximately 100 km/s along FF and enhanced velocity dispersion near the brightest cluster galaxy NGC 3311, suggesting turbulence generated by galaxy-ICM interactions. These results and the compact extent of FF favor fossil plasma supplied by past activity of the brightest cluster galaxy and transported by ICM motions. We also tested whether the measured turbulence could generate or maintain the nonthermal components of FF. For a velocity dispersion of $96.7^{+23.9}_{-24.6}$ km/s and an assumed turbulence scale of 50 kpc, comparable to the Resolve field of view and approximately half the cluster core radius, the turbulent energy flux is approximately $3.49 \times 10^{-28}$ erg cm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. Although this flux may weakly reenergize pre-existing relativistic electrons, the acceleration timescale of approximately 2.5 Gyr exceeds the synchrotron and inverse Compton cooling timescale of approximately 210 Myr. The present turbulence is therefore insufficient to accelerate electrons to high energies. In situ turbulent reacceleration is unlikely to dominate the generation of FF, although it may help maintain fossil electrons supplied by past AGN activity. These results link ICM dynamics to the origin of nonthermal emission and support a time-evolutionary picture of particle acceleration in galaxy clusters.

2611.30321.abstract: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function.

2611.30373.abstract: Lithium-rich (Li-rich) stars are a rare class of objects characterized by an abnormally high Li abundance in their atmospheres. Although several explanations, including binary interactions, have been proposed, their origin remains uncertain. We aim to search for hot companions to the known Li-rich stars in M67, characterize these stars, and evaluate the binary hypothesis as a possible explanation for their Li enhancement. We combined archival ultraviolet photometry from UVIT/AstroSat, GALEX, and Swift/UVOT with optical and infrared photometry to create multiwavelength spectral energy distributions (SEDs) and search for hot companions. We also used high-resolution archival UVES spectra to look for chemical signatures of past binary interactions. Two known Li-rich stars in M67, WOCS6008 and WOCS2003, show a significant far-UV excess relative to a single-star SED fit, attributed to a companion in the former and to stellar activity in the latter. We thus report the first detection of a hot companion to the Li-rich star, WOCS6008, in M67, offering direct evidence of the role of binary interactions in its Li enrichment. The companion is found to be an extremely low-mass (ELM) white dwarf (WD) of $\sim 0.16\pm0.01 M_{\odot}$, consistent with its kinematic mass, and an age of 2.5 Gyr. We find no enhancement of Na or s-process elements and no depletion of C or Mg in WOCS6008, suggesting that mass transfer during the asymptotic giant branch or red giant branch stage is unlikely. Its derived abundances support a scenario in which this star is the accretor in a binary system that underwent early Case B mass transfer. Our results support previous suggestions that stellar rotation is the most favored mechanism for the Li enrichment in this post-interaction system. Overall, the available evidence supports the case for binary interactions as one of the channels to form Li-rich stars.

2611.30393.abstract: The mass of a main-sequence star is usually estimated from its luminosity through a mass--luminosity relation (MLR). This relation depends on metallicity, and its empirical calibration relies on few stars with measured masses. We calibrate the MLR of single main-sequence stars in the Gaia $G$ band as a function of metallicity with $10\,559$ wide binaries. The projected relative speed and separation of a wide binary constrain its total mass statistically. We describe the stellar mass as a monotone function of absolute magnitude and metallicity and fit this function to all pairs. The metallicities come from Gaia low-resolution (XP) spectra and are calibrated by requiring that both stars of a pair have the same metallicity. The likelihood includes the measurement noise, the selection of the sample and pairs with an undetected close companion. The data constrain the MLR over $3.7\lesssim M_{\mathrm{G}} \lesssim11.8$\,mag and $-0.5\lesssim\ \mathrm{[M/H]} \lesssim0.4$, with a median statistical uncertainty of $2.5\%$ in mass. Tests of the model assumptions indicate an additional systematic uncertainty of up to $5\%$. At solar metallicity the MLR agrees with the PARSEC models to within $5\%$. At the faint end, the MIST, BaSTI, Dartmouth and BHAC15 models predict masses 8 to $22\%$ below our MLR. Published masses from orbits, eclipsing binaries and asteroseismology lie within about $10\%$ of our MLR for $M_{\mathrm{G}}<10.5$ mag. For fainter stars they are about $17\%$ lower. The origin of the difference at the faint end is not yet understood. Because a shift of $0.1$ dex in metallicity changes the mass by up to $5\%$, MLRs should be compared on a common metallicity scale.

2611.30696.abstract: EXor variables are a class of young pre-main-sequence stars that show repeated brightenings,likely caused by sudden increases in accretion. Studying their outflow properties, especially during periods of increased activity offers a unique perspective on the accretion-ejection connection in young stars. The aim is to detect and characterise the jet from the prototype EXor variable EX Lupi. Evidence of an outflow driven by EX Lupi has existed for some time but prior to this work, but the jet properties were unknown. This YSO has been monitored for over 100 years and during this time it has undergone increases in magnitude of between 1 and 5 mags which have been connected to increases in the mass accretion rate onto the star. A further aim of this work is to investigate if the jet can be connected to specific accretion events. Spectro-astrometry was applied to UVES spectra collected in 2021 and 2022. HIRES spectra with a similar wavelength range, taken in 2003, 2008 and 2010 were obtained from the Keck Observatory Archive and also analysed with spectro-astrometry. The spatial and kinematic properties of the EX Lupi optical bipolar jet are revealed for the first time. In 2022 the blue-shifted jet is this http URL the same year the red-shifted jet extends to approx 60 au. This finding is significant as it identifies a source that can be used to study the impact of episodes of intense accretion on jet launching. The strongest detection of the jet is in 2010, between the 2008 outburst and the 2022 burst, which points to a new ejection event triggered by the 2008 outburst. Evidence of enhanced ejection connected to a 2002 burst is also presented. No change in the jet is observed during the 2022 burst. However, we are hindered here by the limitations of the technique.

2611.31130.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.

2611.31204.title: JAISP: A Joint Rubin-Euclid Foundation Model for Cross-Instrument Source Detection and Astrometry

2611.31204.abstract: Joint pixel-level processing of Rubin and Euclid imaging promises deeper source detection and the cross-survey consistency that precision cosmology requires. We introduce JAISP (Joint AI Survey Processing), a foundation model that learns a single representation of ten-band imaging: Rubin ugrizy and Euclid VIS, Y, J, and H, from the first public releases over $\approx 0.2$ deg$^2$ of the ECDFS deep field. Trained without labels by predicting each band from the other nine, its frozen encoder drives small task-specific networks for source detection and astrometry. The detection network recovers nearly all VIS-selected Euclid Q1 catalog sources on held-out sky, and source injection shows that combining all ten bands extends the point-source detection limit by $\approx 0.3$ mag beyond VIS alone. The astrometry network transfers the sharp VIS localization to the other nine bands, reducing median cross-band positional offsets from $\approx 50$ to $6$--$10$ mas while retaining the full precision of its VIS centroid anchor even for faint sources. Separating this per-source scatter exposes the cross-survey concordance field: a coherent $9$--$10$ mas offset between the two independently Gaia-registered astrometric solutions, dominated by a component common to all bands. Applied without retraining to a second Euclid Deep Field, both networks perform without measurable loss. These gains serve the joint-survey science case: a deeper census recovers faint neighbors whose blending biases weak-lensing shapes and photometric redshifts, and VIS-grade positions in every band supply the common astrometric reference that joint photometry and faint-source proper motions require. A single representation learned once from survey pixels thus serves several measurements across the sky.
